dimensions.title: Goal Alignment & Deep Why
dimensions.absenceStatement: 3 of 4 required behaviours are not evidenced in the transcript. 1 required behaviour(s) have both supporting and contradicting evidence, so they cannot be treated as established.
dimensions.reasoning: At L44 Ivan asks the single goal question — "what are you hoping to get out of this?" — gets "walk without the pain" at L45, and at L46 immediately generalises it into a category statement about "our plantar fasciitis clients" before pivoting to logistics at L48. That is the textbook Mid pattern: ask goals, accept the first physical answer, no probing. The client repeatedly opens emotional doors — L23 "it's been a lot more than just the foot thing", L37 "I've tried so many things on my own", L75 "there's been a lot going on where I just kind of lose —", L85 "is this gonna actually be different" — and each time she is cut off mid-sentence and redirected to program mechanics or reassurance. No "why is that important to you", no impact question, no 30-day success metric (Friday video upload is a logistics deadline, not a success metric), no North Star statement, and therefore no client confirmation. The goal is never referenced again after L46.
dimensions.quickFix: After Renata says she wants to walk without pain (L45), stop and dig: "Why does that matter to you — what does pain-free walking give you back?" and follow her opening at L23/L75 ("a lot more than just the foot thing") with a second why to surface the identity driver (nurse who can finish a shift, be present off-shift). Then reflect it back as a North Star — "What I hear you saying is you want to be the nurse who finishes a twelve-hour shift and still has something left for her own life" — get an explicit "yes, that's exactly it", and pin a concrete 30-day metric (e.g. "by day 30, first ten steps out of bed are under a 3/10"), then reference it again in the recap at L104.

dimensions.reasoning: At L40 Ivan names all three canonical phases in correct order — Retraining, Remodeling, Integrating — which is fully creditable phase identification. dimensions.quickFix: When Renata asked "what's the difference between them" at L41, answer it: give one sentence of outcome per phase tied to her goal — e.g. "Retraining: calm the plantar tissue and fix how you load the foot so hour six of a shift stops spiking; Remodeling: load the calf and foot to build real tissue capacity; Integrating: put that capacity back into twelve hours on your feet." Add an analogy (foundation → walls → roof) plus a reassessment cadence ("we recheck your videos at week 4, 8 and 12"), then close with "does that make sense as a path?" and get explicit confirmation.

dimensions.title: Journey & Expectation Setting
dimensions.absenceStatement: 3 of 5 required behaviours are not evidenced in the transcript. 2 required behaviour(s) have both supporting and contradicting evidence, so they cannot be treated as established.
dimensions.reasoning: At L84 Ivan does gesture at emotional friction — "some weeks feel like nothing's happening. That's pretty normal honestly" — and Renata responds by opening up about her fear that this won't be different (L85). That is the one genuine moment of expectation setting, but Ivan immediately pivots to reassurance about the protocol (L86) rather than sitting with the valley, naming a specific window (weeks 3–4), or telling her what to do when it hits. Elsewhere the call is logistical: phases are named but not explained (L42 explicitly defers), timeline is delivery-focused (videos Friday, program Monday). There is no distinction between good discomfort and bad pain, no framing of month one as foundational rather than transformational, and no link back to a North Star — indeed no North Star was constructed at all; her "walk without pain" goal at L45 was generalised and dropped. When she raises her real adherence worry at L75 ("there's been a lot going on where I just kind of lose —") Ivan answers with scheduling flexibility, not psychological prep. So: expectations exist but are mostly informational, with one brief, un-developed normalization. That is above pure vagueness but well short of Strong's "timeline explained, structure ok" plus physical-discomfort normalization — the structure was explicitly not explained and discomfort was never addressed. This sits at the top of Mid.
dimensions.quickFix: Explicitly walk the emotional arc: "Month one is foundational, not transformational — you probably won't feel dramatically better by day 30, and that's the plan working. Around week 3–4 most people hit a valley where it feels like nothing's changing; that's exactly when I want you to message me instead of going quiet." Then separate good discomfort (calf/foot working, fades within a day) from bad pain (sharp heel pain that's worse the next morning — stop and tell me). Explain what each of the three phases actually feels like rather than deferring it. Finally, tie it to her stated goal: "At week 8 I'm going to ask you whether you're starting to walk without thinking about every step" — and check she's heard it.
